inline.s: “Good man! The sky is not really filled with flowers; it is the false grasping of one with diseased eyes. Because of this false grasping, not only do they mistake this empty self-nature, they also delude themselves about the place where the flowers truly arise. From this false existence they revolve in birth and death; therefore it is called ignorance.”

Good man! In truth there are no flowers in the sky; this is the illusion falsely grasped by the diseased eye. Because of false grasping, not only do they falsely grasp the sky as substantially existing, they also think there truly are flowers that arise from it. Because sentient beings, through inverted confusion, falsely take the illusion-manifested body and mind to be real and cling to them as self, they revolve in birth and death without end; therefore it is called ignorance.
[Not only mistaking this self-nature of emptiness] wrongly thinking that emptiness has a self-nature. In truth all dharmas are without self-nature (see
The Real Nature of All Dharmas

), so emptiness too has no self-nature. [Without self-nature] means that all dharmas have no real substance of their own; it is also called no nature. [Not only mistaking this self-nature of emptiness, they also delude themselves about the place where the real flowers arise] Not only do they falsely grasp emptiness as really existing (as substance), they also think there truly are flowers arising from it.
Q: If all dharmas are without self-nature, why is it said that sentient beings have self-nature?

A: The word self-nature has two meanings in Buddhist learning: first, the wondrous, luminous, all-virtuous spiritual capacity, which is the self-nature of sentient beings; second, a real substance. The meaning of “all dharmas are without self-nature” is that all dharmas have no real substance, being all illusions, like the matters of a dream. Without self-nature is also called no nature. The Treatise on Consciousness-only says: “All dharmas are without self-nature.” The Lotus Sutra says: “Know that all dharmas are ever without nature.” The Surangama Sutra says: “All illusions become without nature.”
Q: Why is it that when one falsely grasps the four great elements as one’s own body and the shadow of the six objects as one’s own mind, one revolves in birth and death?
A: Because we sentient beings are all within the dream of transmigration (about the dream of transmigration, see
The Real Nature of All Dharmas

, the chapter on “the dream of ignorance”). If one takes this body (the four elements) and this mind (the shadow of the six objects) as self, then feelings of love and aversion arise. Following the feelings one creates karma, and through karma one receives retribution, so birth and death revolve without rest. If one wishes to escape this dream of birth-after-birth and death-after-death, one must accomplish it through cultivation. The common path is to cut off all afflictions, and at the moment of death be able to be master; then one can end birth and death and escape transmigration. The founder Huangbo’s Essential of Mind Transmission says:

“Whenever a man approaches the end, he should contemplate the five aggregates as empty, the four elements as without self, the true mind as without mark, neither going nor coming. At birth the nature does not come; at death the nature does not go. Serenely extinct, mind and realm as one. If one can thus directly, in an instant, understand, and not be bound by the three times, this is a man who has gone beyond the world.”
If one cultivates the Pure Land gate, one needs only the ten recollections at death to be continuous (see
The Conditions for Rebirth
), and one will sense Amitabha Buddha coming to receive and guide, escaping this dream of transmigration and being reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

“Good man! This ignorance has no real substance. Like a man in a dream - while he dreams, the dream is not nothing, but when he wakes he gains nothing at all. Like the many flowers in the sky, which vanish in the sky - one cannot say there is a fixed place where they vanish. Why? Because there is no place from which they arise. All sentient beings, within the unborn, falsely see arising and ceasing; therefore it is called revolving in birth and death.”

Good man! This ignorance is not really existent. Like a man in a dream - while he dreams, the matters of the dream are not nothing, but when he wakes, all is gone. If the eye-disease is cured (the metaphor of awaking from the dream of ignorance), the many sky-flowers vanish in the sky, and one cannot say there is a definite place of extinction. Why? Because the sky-flowers never arose to begin with - how could there be a place of extinction? All sentient beings, within the original state where not a single thing exists, falsely see arising and ceasing; this falsely-seen arising and ceasing is what is called revolving in birth and death (the divided birth-and-death and the transformation birth-and-death).

This means: the revolving of birth and death is like the matters of a dream - it is the illusion that sentient beings, from beginningless time, falsely grasping the five aggregates’ body and mind, have set up.

[Revolving in birth and death] revolving in the divided birth-and-death and the transformation birth-and-death. [Divided birth-and-death] For sentient beings within the three realms and six destinies, because they are sensed by good and evil karma, each has a limited lifespan and a delimited body, so their birth and death is called “divided birth-and-death.” One who ends divided birth-and-death has escaped transmigration. [Transformation birth-and-death] For the sages of the three vehicles, having already cut off the delusions of views and thought and ended divided birth-and-death, during the process of cultivation their deluded thoughts gradually pass away and their realization gradually grows; this movement of delusion and awakening is different in each stage, and the passing from one stage to the next is like a single birth-and-death; its changes are so wondrous, subtle and inconceivable that it is called “transformation birth-and-death.” One who ends transformation birth-and-death perfectly realizes the Buddha-fruit.

“Good man! Those Tathagatas who, on the stage of cause, cultivate complete enlightenment, knowing that these are sky-flowers, have no revolving, and have no body and mind to undergo that birth and death. It is not by contrivance that it is non-existent; it is because the fundamental nature is non-existent.”

Good man! Those Tathagatas who, on the stage of cause, cultivate the complete-enlightenment gate, knowing that all this arising and ceasing is illusion (this sutra uses the metaphor of sky-flowers for illusion), have no revolving in birth and death; and knowing body and mind to be illusory, they have no body or mind to undergo birth and death. This is not a non-existence after contrivance, because body, mind, birth and death never existed to begin with. (This speaks of the real nature of all dharmas: all dharmas are ultimately empty, all non-existent. See
The Real Nature of All Dharmas

“Those who know this consciousness are like empty space. Those who know emptiness are the mark of sky-flowers. Nor can it be said: there is no knowing nature. Both existence and non-existence are dispatched; this is called pure awareness in accordance. Why? Because of the nature of emptiness, because of ever being unmoving, because in the Tathagata-store there is no arising or ceasing, because there is no knowing or seeing, like the nature of the Dharma-realm, ultimately complete and perfect, pervading the ten directions. This is called the dharma-practice of the stage of cause. Bodhisattvas, by this, in the Great Vehicle give rise to the pure mind; sentient beings of the last age, cultivating in accord with this, do not fall into wrong views.”

That person who knows the sky-flowers are illusory is like empty space, equally unmoving (equally regarding everything, neither bewildered nor drawn by illusions). Knowing that the myriads of forms are like empty space, with not a single thing, they empty away the mark of the sky-flowers. But it also cannot be said that there is no mark of the sky-flowers. Both existence (falsely grasping dharmas as real) and non-existence (denying that dharmas have marks) are dispatched; this is called pure awareness in accordance (neither attached to existence nor falling into emptiness). Why? Because of the reason that empty space has not a single thing, because of the reason of being serene and unmoving, because of the reason that in the Tathagata-store there is no arising or ceasing, because of the reason of no knowing or seeing, because of the reason that the Dharma-realm is ultimately complete and pervading the ten directions. This is called the Tathagata’s dharma-practice of the stage of cause. Bodhisattvas, by this, give rise to the pure mind in the Great Vehicle; sentient beings of the last age, cultivating by this, do not fall into wrong views.

[Those who know this consciousness are like empty space] That person who knows the sky-flowers are illusory is like empty space, equally unmoving (equally regarding everything, neither bewildered nor drawn by illusions). The verse later says: “The awakened are like empty space, equally unmoving.” [That is the mark of sky-flowers] That is, empty away this illusory mark of the sky-flowers. Here “empty” is a verb. [Pure awareness] The mind-substance without defilement is called pure; not deluded toward the objects is called awareness. [In accordance] according with conditions and circumstances. [Pure awareness in accordance] pure awareness and in accordance. Neither attached to existence nor falling into emptiness. This is the Great Vehicle’s orthodox teaching that the Buddha revealed in the Diamond Sutra: universally ferrying sentient beings to Buddhahood, yet not attached to the mark of ferrying them. Compassion and emptiness working together, compassionately ferrying beings yet not attached to the mark. The Diamond Sutra says:

“All the many kinds of living beings - whether born from eggs, from a womb, from moisture, or by transformation, whether with form or without form, whether with perception or without perception, whether neither with perception nor without perception - I cause them all to enter the nirvana of no remainder and cross them over; thus crossing over innumerable, countless, boundless living beings, in truth no living being is crossed over.”
(see
The Diamond Sutra Explained

) [Because there is no knowing or seeing] Here “knowing and seeing” refers to the views established by way of deliberation and discrimination. This differs from wisdom; wisdom is the non-discriminating prajna.

[Dharma-realm] In terms of phenomenal marks, dharma means the various dharmas and realm means boundaries: all the things of the phenomenal world each have their distinct, different marks and cannot be confused, called the “phenomenal Dharma-realm.” In terms of the principle-substance, though the various dharmas are endlessly different in outer marks, they share one nature (ultimately empty, all non-existent), called the “principle Dharma-realm.”

Then the World-Honored One, wishing to re-declare this meaning, spoke in verse: Manjushri, you should know: all Tathagatas, having fully penetrated ignorance and known it to be like sky-flowers, are able to escape the flow. Again, like a man in a dream, when he wakes nothing can be obtained.”

Then the World-Honored One, wishing to re-declare the meaning of the above instruction, spoke in verse: Manjushri, you should know: all Buddhas, fully awakened to ignorance and knowing all dharmas to be like sky-flowers, illusory and unreal, are able to escape the flow (referring to escaping the divided birth-and-death and the transformation birth-and-death). Again, like a man in a dream - after the great dream wakes, where is the man in the dream?
[Again, like a man in a dream, when he wakes nothing can be obtained] This is what Mazu called “not mind, not Buddha.” The Exposition of the Five Lamps records:
“A monk asked: ‘Why does the Master say, “Mind is Buddha”?’ The Master
(Mazu)
said: ‘To stop the infant’s crying’
(this is the expedient saying for those new to the study)
.’ He asked: ‘When the crying stops, then what?’ The Master said: ‘Not mind, not Buddha.’ He said: ‘For those who come beyond these two kinds, how do you indicate?’ The Master said: ‘Tell him
(him)
it is not a thing.’”
The Exposition of the Five Lamps further says:
“The Chan master Zizai of Funiu Mountain at Yique, of the Li family of Wuxing, first followed the master Guoyi, and after full ordination studied under Mazu and awakened the mind-ground
(enlightenment)
. Mazu had him deliver a letter to the National Master Zhong
(the National Master Huizhong)
. The National Master asked: ‘What Dharma does the great master Ma use to show his disciples?’ He said: ‘Mind is Buddha.’ The National Master said: ‘What sort of words are those’
(he greatly disapproved)
!’ After a long while
(a long time passed)

he asked again: ‘Besides this, is there any further teaching?’ The Master said: ‘Not mind, not Buddha. Or it is said: not mind, not Buddha, not a thing.’ The National Master said: ‘That is a little better’
(that is about right)

[To stop the infant’s crying] a metaphor for the expedient teaching (not the ultimate teaching). When a child cries, an adult gives him a yellow poplar leaf, saying: “This is a piece of gold; you may take it and buy sweets.” The child holds it and stops crying. The Mahaparinirvana Sutra says: “As when an infant cries, the parents give it a yellow poplar leaf and say: ‘Do not cry! Do not cry! I shall give you gold.’ The infant, seeing it, gives rise to the thought of real gold and stops crying; yet this poplar leaf is not really gold.”

In the above kōan, three levels are spoken of: “mind is Buddha,” “not mind, not Buddha,” and “not mind, not Buddha, not a thing.” The mind spoken of here refers to the self-nature. “Mind is Buddha” means that Buddha is nothing else; the perfectly awakened self-nature is the Buddha. “Not mind, not Buddha” means that self-nature and Buddha are both illusions - matters in the dream of ignorance. “Not mind, not Buddha, not a thing” speaks of the “that” which is dreaming the dream of ignorance.

“The awakened are like empty space, equally unmoving; awareness pervading the ten directions is to accomplish the Buddha-way. The many illusions have no place of extinction; accomplishing the way is also no attainment, because the fundamental nature is complete. Bodhisattvas within this can give rise to the bodhi mind; sentient beings of the last age, cultivating this, avoid wrong views.”

The awakened, like the serene stillness of empty space, equally regard all dharmas (because they are equally all illusions), unmoved and unturned by them; thus awareness pervading the ten directions, they accomplish the Buddha-way. When the many illusions pass away there is no place of extinction; having accomplished the Buddha-way there is also no attainment, because the fundamental nature is complete. Bodhisattvas within this can give rise to the bodhi mind; sentient beings of the last age, cultivating thus, do not fall into wrong views.

[The many illusions have no place of extinction] When the many illusions pass away there is no place of extinction; because the many illusions never arose to begin with, so when they pass away, where could there be a place of extinction? [Accomplishing the way also no attainment] Accomplishing the way is also a matter in the dream of ignorance, hence it is said to be no attainment. [Giving rise to the bodhi mind] Giving rise to the bodhi mind, in full, is giving rise to the anuttara-samyak-sambodhi mind, also abbreviated as giving rise to the mind. Mr. Liu Zhuyuan says: “The bodhi mind is the pure self-nature mind. This pure self-nature mind is equal in beings and Buddhas, possessed by everyone, neither increasing nor decreasing. To give rise means to set it going, to develop it. Giving rise to the bodhi mind is to set going and develop the pure self-nature mind. At the beginning it is only setting it going; seeing the nature is the developing.” (see
The Essentials of Baiyun

) The master Guifeng says: “To see the four elements as broken illusions, to penetrate the six objects as sky-flowers, to awaken that one’s own mind is the Buddha mind, and to see the fundamental nature as the Dharma nature - this is giving rise to the mind.” (The Transmission of the Lamp)

blocks.text: 1. How to be free of the illusory

inline.s: “Then Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, in the midst of the assembly, rose from his seat, bowed at the Buddha’s feet, circled him three times to the right, knelt with palms together, and said to the Buddha: Great compassionate World-Honored One, I pray that for the bodhisattvas of this assembly and for all the sentient beings of the last age who cultivate the Great Vehicle, having heard this realm of pure complete enlightenment, you will tell how they should cultivate.”

Then Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, in the midst of the assembly, rose from his seat, bowed at the Buddha’s feet, circled him three times to the right, knelt with palms joined, and respectfully said to the Buddha: Great compassionate World-Honored One, I pray that you will preach for the bodhisattvas of this assembly and for all the sentient beings of the last age who cultivate the Great Vehicle, how, having heard this realm of pure complete enlightenment, they are to cultivate in order to reach it.

“World-Honored One, if these sentient beings know that things are illusory, then body and mind are also illusory; why do they, with illusion, still cultivate within illusion? If the nature of all illusions entirely ceases, then there is no mind; who is it that cultivates? How again can one speak of cultivating as illusory? If these sentient beings originally do not cultivate, abiding long among the transformations of birth and death, and never comprehend the illusory realm, how can the deluded mind be liberated? I pray that for all sentient beings of the last age you will show what expedient means, progressively cultivated, cause them to be forever free of all illusions. Having spoken, he fell prostrate on the ground. Thus three times he begged, ending and beginning again.”

World-Honored One, if they know that all dharmas are illusory, then body and mind are also illusory; since it is so, why do they still use illusion to cultivate within illusion? If the nature of all illusions entirely ceases, then there is no mind - then for whom is this cultivation? Why again is it said that cultivation is like illusion? If these sentient beings do not cultivate at all, then abiding long among the transformations of birth and death, they will never comprehend that this whole realm is an illusory realm; how then can the deluded mind be liberated? I pray that for all sentient beings of the last age you will reveal what good, skilful means, progressively cultivated, will cause them to be forever free of all illusions. When Samantabhadra Bodhisattva had finished this speech, he fell prostrate on the ground. Thus three times he begged, ending and beginning again.

[If these sentient beings] if those sentient beings. Here “sentient beings” includes the bodhisattvas of this assembly and all the sentient beings of the last age who cultivate the Great Vehicle. Within the ten Dharma-realms, apart from the Buddha, the nine realms of sentient beings (hells, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, humans, heavens, sravakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas) are all called sentient beings. [Who is it that cultivates] that is, for whom is the cultivation. The “for whom” is inverted to “who is it for” to strengthen the tone. For example: who does it for whom. [Expedient means] the skilful, accommodating means, methods or speech used to transform sentient beings. “Expedient” is relative to “real” and “ultimate”; it means setting up the teaching according to capacity.

blocks.text: 2. Knowing the illusory is to be free of it

inline.s: “Then the World-Honored One said to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva: Excellent! Excellent! Good man. You have been able, for the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, to ask about practicing the bodhisattvas’ samadhi of the illusory, and the progressive expedient means, causing sentient beings to be free of all illusions. Listen attentively now; I shall speak it for you. At that time Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, receiving the instruction with joy, and all the assembly, listened in silence.”

Then the World-Honored One said to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva: Excellent! Excellent! Good man. You have been able, for the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, to ask about the method of practicing the samadhi of the illusory and the progressive sequence of cultivation, causing sentient beings to be free of all illusions. Now still your minds and listen attentively; I shall preach it for you. At that time Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, receiving the instruction with joy, and all the assembly, listened in silence.

“Good man! All the various illusory transformations of sentient beings all arise within the Tathagata’s wondrous mind of complete enlightenment, like sky-flowers arising from the sky. Though the illusory flowers pass away, the empty nature is not destroyed. The illusory mind of sentient beings still passes away in dependence on the illusory; when all illusions are entirely extinguished, the mind of awareness does not move. To speak of awareness in dependence on illusion, this too is called illusion. If one says there is awareness, one has not yet left illusion. For one who says there is no awareness, it is likewise. Therefore when illusion is extinguished, this is called unmoving.”
